hints: Look carefully at the three terms and ask yourself which big process each one belongs to, growth and copying, nuclear division, or splitting the cytoplasm.
Remember the full Cambridge definition: cell cycle = interphase + mitosis (which starts with prophase) + cytokinesis.
walkthrough:
**Recall What the Cell Cycle Covers**

Think of the cell cycle as the whole life story of a dividing cell, from when it is made to when it divides into two. It is not just mitosis, it includes everything in order.

**Check Each Event Against That Definition**

1 interphase is the long growth phase where DNA is replicated. 2 prophase is the first stage of mitosis, when chromosomes condense. 3 cytokinesis is the final splitting of the cytoplasm into two daughter cells.

**Put It All Together**

Since interphase, mitosis (including prophase) and cytokinesis are all regular, repeating parts of the cycle, all three statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. That points straight to option A.

options.A: Correct and reassuring. Interphase, prophase (as part of mitosis) and cytokinesis are all essential, repeating stages of the cell cycle.
options.B: Close but incomplete. It correctly includes interphase and prophase but wrongly leaves out cytokinesis, which completes cell division.
options.C: Incomplete. It correctly includes interphase and cytokinesis but wrongly leaves out prophase, which is the first stage of mitosis.
options.D: Incomplete. It correctly includes prophase and cytokinesis but wrongly leaves out interphase, which is the longest part of the cycle.
